outcome: Maternal morbidity (postpartum hemorrhage, blood transfusion, uterine rupture, ICU admittance, death)
cohort: A cohort of 2592 women with one previous caesarean section, a singleton pregnancy, who delivered at or after 37 weeks, and had no contraindication for vaginal delivery.
finding: The developed prediction models for morbidity following trial of labour or elective repeat caesarean section showed insufficient performance with poor discriminative capacity.
mod_finding: Total morbidity was higher in women choosing Trial of Labour (TOL) compared to Elective Repeat Caesarean Section (ERCS), but individual prediction models for morbidity based on different delivery modes were not successfully developed.
